answer: To earn weight, an identity must run a sequential memory-hard proof chained to its own non-transferable tenure: every step needs the memory state produced by the previous step, so the work cannot be split across clones or run in parallel. A new head begins at dawn with no history, and no bridge transfers tenure from an old identity to a new one — each copper token of earned tenure stays welded to the identity that did the work. Splitting into n clones therefore means n full sequential proofs, each restarting from zero, while one honest identity keeps compounding.
